d.d: In the state of being active, functioning or operating.
d.x: All the lights are on, so they must be home.

d.d: Happening; taking place; being or due to be put into action.
d.x: We had to ration our food because there was a war on.

d.d: Of a person, used to express agreement to or acceptance of a proposal or challenge made by that person; most commonly with subject "you" (see you're on).
d.x: "Five bucks says the Cavs win tonight." ―"You're on!"

d.d: So as to cover or be fitted.
d.x: The lid wasn't screwed on properly.
The policeman moved the tramp on.

d.d: Positioned at the upper surface of, touching from above.
d.x: A vase of flowers stood on the table.

d.d: Positioned at or resting against the outer surface of; attached to.
d.x: He had a scar on the side of his face.
He wore old shoes on his feet.

d.d: In the Japanese language, a pronunciation, or reading, of a kanji character that was originally based on the character's pronunciation in Chinese, contrasted with kun.
d.x: Most kanji have two kinds of reading, called "on" and "kun".
